After a screening phase of up to 4 weeks, the patients were randomized in 1:1:1 ratio to one of the three treatment groups to receive daily doses of placebo, Teriflunomide 7 mg, or Teriflunomide 14 mg.

endpoint.text: Annualized relapse rate (ARR), defined as the number of confirmed relapses per patient-year

citations.quote: The primary efficacy variable was the annualized relapse rate (ARR), defined as the number of confirmed relapses per patient-year.
A total of 1338 patients were screened and 1088 patients were randomized.
The ITT patient population for this study consisted of 1086 subjects.

result.text: Adjusted ARR 0.539 (placebo), 0.370 (7 mg), 0.369 (14 mg); relative risk reduction 31.2% (p=0.0002) for 7 mg and 31.5% (p=0.0005) for 14 mg. Disability progression sustained for 12 weeks was significantly reduced only in the 14 mg group (20.2% vs 27.3% placebo, p=0.028, hazard ratio 0.70); 7 mg not significant (21.7%, p=0.084, hazard ratio 0.76).

citations.quote: The adjusted ARR was 0.539 (95% CI: 0.466 to 0.623) in the placebo group, 0.370 (95% CI: 0.318 to 0.432) in the Teriflunomide 7 mg group, and 0.369 (95% CI: 0.308 to 0.441) in the Teriflunomide 14 mg group. These results corresponded to a relative risk reduction of 31.2% (p=0.0002) in the Teriflunomide 7 mg group and 31.5% (p=0.0005) in the Teriflunomide 14 mg group compared to placebo.

The time to disability progression sustained for 12 weeks (as measured by at least a 1-point increase from baseline EDSS \le 5.5 or a 0.5 point increase for those with a baseline EDSS > 5.5) was statistically significantly reduced only in the teriflunomide 14 mg group compared to placebo (see Table 2 and Figure 1).

detail.text: WARNING: HEPATOTOXICITY and RISK OF TERATOGENICITY — severe liver injury including fatal liver failure has been reported with leflunomide and a similar risk is expected for teriflunomide; AUBAGIO may cause major birth defects and is contraindicated in pregnant women or women of childbearing potential not using reliable contraception.

citations.quote: ## WARNING: HEPATOTOXICITY and RISK OF TERATOGENICITY*See full prescribing information for complete boxed warning*

Based on animal data, AUBAGIO may cause major birth defects if used during pregnancy. AUBAGIO is contraindicated in pregnant women or women of childbearing potential who are not using reliable contraception. Pregnancy must be avoided during AUBAGIO treatment. (4.2, 5.2)
